turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hey, come on in. Uh, this screen keeps freezing, sorry. What brings you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Lump in my groin. I sat out there forever and I'm wiped, so can we just do this.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): A lump. I clicked the wrong chart. Which side, tell me again?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Right groin. I already told them at the desk.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right groin. How long has it been going on?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Three months. It started small.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Uh, say that again? This fan is loud and I lost the line.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Three months. I'm not saying it a third time.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ok. When do you actually notice it?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I told you, three months. When I lift boxes and pallets the right groin pops out. I lie down and it's gone.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Out with lifting, gone when you lie down. Does it hurt?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Mild ache in the groin by evening. Not a sharp pain.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does that ache wake you up at night?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): I won't put that down as a yes. Any vomiting?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No vomiting.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about nausea?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes, not really. Eating is fine.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cough or shortness of breath?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Nope. Breathing is fine.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): What do you do for work?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Warehouse. I load trucks, heavy manual stuff, all day. The boss still wants those pallets moved.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Other problems, blood pressure, diabetes, anything?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): High blood pressure for eight years. No diabetes. Could you stop scrolling while I talk.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse put in your meds. It says metoporol 50 milligrams twice a day. Is that right?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It's 25 milligrams, twice a day. She typed 50. I watched her.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hold on, the cursor jumped. Umm, give me the dose again.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): 25. Twice a day. Metoprolol. Not 50.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll flag it. Are you taking it every day?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else, even from the drugstore?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Two advil, 200 milligrams each, in the evening when the ache is there.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines, food, anything at all?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No allergies.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Surgeries in the past?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never had surgery.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or drink?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't smoke. A beer on the weekend, that's all. You planning to look at the lump?
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yeah, lie back. Right groin. Cough for me.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Cough. It shows more if I stand, just so you actually see it.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Soft bulge in the right inguinal canal, and it reduces when you're flat. Skin isn't red, abdomen is soft, not really tender.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Goes away lying down. I said that.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure is 136 over 84, uh, pulse 78.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. I've got a shift later, so what's the verdict.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Most likely a right inguinal hernia. It comes out when you lift and goes back lying down. The surgeon should confirm it, I'm not calling that final.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): A hernia. Figures.

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm referring you to general surgery today, they'll set that visit up. Thursday morning the nurse takes bloods at 8, fasting, nothing to eat or drink after midnight. Blood count and chemistry, for the pre-op.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday at 8, fasting. I'll be there. Don't love the early part.

[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): If those are borderline we do a third test, a clotting study, only if they're borderline. If the lump stops going back in or this doesn't settle, then we get an ultrasound, and I'm not ordering that now.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Whatever. Just tell me the rules.

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): No heavy lifting till you're seen, stay off the pallets. If it gets stuck and you start vomiting, that's the ER. I'll see you back in this clinic in two weeks with the lab results.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, no lifting, Thursday bloods. Type it in right, I'm not repeating it at the desk.

spec.situation: Manual worker with a groin lump that appears on lifting and goes away lying down; mild ache by evening; no vomiting; surgical referral planned, advice on lifting.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Transcript says abdomen 'not really tender'; right groin site not stated.

omissions.text: Metoprolol dose should be recorded as 25 mg twice a day; the current medication entry omits the dose, and the transcript explicitly corrects an erroneous 50 mg twice-daily charted dose.
Nausea was discussed and was not clearly absent: patient said 'Sometimes, not really. Eating is fine,' indicating equivocal/intermittent nausea rather than a negative finding.
Mild groin ache was described as 'not a sharp pain.'
Night waking from the ache was equivocal: when asked if the ache wakes him at night, patient said 'Sometimes, not really,' and the doctor said he would not record it as yes.
Physical exam finding that the groin bulge reduces when the patient is flat/lying down was stated by the doctor during examination.
The surgeon/general surgery visit is to confirm the diagnosis; doctor stated he was not calling the hernia diagnosis final.
Follow-up is specifically in this clinic in two weeks with the lab results.
